- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.44) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate during sustained negative sentiment (sentiment <0.18) — model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Lagged mean reversion: model often overreacts to recent highs/lows, then drifts toward historical mean too slowly.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model forecasts peak too early and then overcorrects downward.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is rising (0.36+), model tends to overforecast; when falling (0.18-), underforecast.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum, especially when sentiment is volatile.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — model often mirrors sentiment trends without accounting for structural market constraints or policy shifts.
